Thiraphong Chansiri (Executive Chairman) | industry = [[Food]] | products = [[Seafood]] ([[Frozen Food|frozen]], [[Canned food|canned]], chilled) | services = | revenue = {{increase}} 140 billion [[baht]] (2017) | operating_income = | net_income = {{increase}} 6 billion baht | assets = {{increase}} 146.3 billion baht | equity = {{increase}} 48.2 billion baht | owner = | num_employees = 49,000 (2017) | parent = | divisions = | subsidiaries = | website = {{URL|http://www.thaiunion.com/}} | footnotes = | intl = }} '''Thai Union Group PCL''' is a Thailand-based producer of seafood based products. It was founded in 1977,{{cite book |title=Annual Report 2017 |date=2018|publisher=Thai Union Group Public Company Limited |location=Samut Sakhon |edition=English|url=http://tu.listedcompany.com/misc/ar/20180329-tu-ar2017-en.pdf|accessdate=20 June 2018}} and was listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) on 22 November 1994. Thai Union operates worldwide with plant facilities in France, Germany, Ghana, Poland, Portugal, Papua New Guinea, Norway, Seychelles, Scotland, Vietnam, Thailand and the United States. Its business includes tuna, shrimp, sardines, mackerel, salmon, pet food and prepared foods.{{cite news |last1=Apisitniran |first1=Lamonphet |title=Thai Union cheers record sales, profit |url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/business/news/875884/thai-union-cheers-record-sales-profit |accessdate=20 June 2018 |work=Bangkok Post |date=2016-02-25}} == Brand portfolio == Thai Union's brand portfolio includes: * Bellotta (business in Thailand) * [[Chicken of the Sea]] (business in the US) * Fisho (business in Thailand) * [[John West Foods|John West]] (business in the Netherlands and the UK) * [[King Oscar (company)|King Oscar]] (business in Norway) * Mareblu (business in Italy) * Marvo (business in Thailand) * Parmentier (business in France) * {{ill|Petit Navire|fr|vertical-align=sup}} (business in France) * {{ill|Rügen Fisch|de|vertical-align=sup}} (business in Germany) * Sealect (business in Thailand) == Financial performance == In 2017, the Thai Union had revenues of 140 billion [[Thai baht|baht]], with a net profit of six billion baht. Total assets amounted to 146.3 billion baht. Total shareholder equity was 48.2 billion baht.{{RP|24-25}} Thai Union's target was to achieve US$8 billion in revenue by 2020. The revenue contribution of its different businesses as of 2017 were:{{cite web |title=Management Discussion and Analysis for 2017 Results |url=http://tu.listedcompany.com/misc/investor_note/20180220-tu-investor-note-fy2017-en.pdf |website=Thai Union Group Public Company Limited |publisher=Thai Union |accessdate=20 June 2018}}{{RP|5}} * Ambient seafood business, 45 percent * Frozen and chilled seafood and related business, 42 percent * PetCare, value-added and others, 13 percent == History == * 1977: Established on 17 March 1977 as Asian Pacific Thai Tuna Co, Ltd. with an initial capital of 25 million baht.{{cite web|title=Company History|url=http://www.thaiunion.com/en/about/company/company-history|website=Thai Union|accessdate=16 December 2016}} * 1988: Renamed Thai Union Frozen Products PLC in March 1988. * 2010: Acquired MW Brands (now Thai Union Europe) from [[Trilantic Capital Partners]] for €680 million. * 2010: Expanded and diversified into the pet food business with U.S. Pet Nutrition LLC. * 2013: Became the first Thai company to join the [[United Nations Global Compact|UN Global Compact]], an initiative aimed at "promoting sustainable and socially responsible policies."{{cite news|url=http://www.bangkokpost.com/business/news/362812/tuf-becomes-signatory-to-un-global-compact|title=TUF becomes signatory to UN Global Compact |work=Bangkok Post|date=2013-08-03|accessdate=21 June 2018}} * 2013: Became a founding member of the [[International Seafood Sustainability Foundation]] (ISSF). * 2014: Signed a deal for MW Brands to take over 40-year-old French company MerAlliance, the fourth-largest [[smoked salmon]] producer in Europe. MerAlliance's revenue for the year to 31 March 2014 was US$220 million. * 2014–2017: Included in the [[Dow Jones Sustainability Indices|Dow Jones Sustainability Indices (DJSI)]] for four consecutive years, with the company ranked in the 97th percentile among companies in the industry.{{cite news|url=http://www.bangkokpost.com/business/finance/1091276/thai-firms-lead-asean-peers-in-sustainability-gauges|title=Thai firms lead Asean peers in sustainability gauges |work=Bangkok seafood importer and distributor in the US. * 2006: Established Chicken of the Sea Frozen Foods to market frozen seafood in the US. Chicken of the Sea Frozen Foods later merged with Empress International and was renamed Tri-Union Frozen Products, Inc. * 2006: Acquired majority stake in PT Jui Fa International Food, a canned tuna MerAlliance, Europe's fourth smoked salmon producer and number one producer in France. * 2014: Acquired [[King Oscar sardines|King Oscar]] AS of Norway, a shelf-stable sardine brand in Norway, USA, Lobster|url=http://fortune.com/2016/10/11/thai-union-red-lobster-deal/|accessdate=22 December 2016|work=Fortune|agency=Reuters|date=2016-10-16}} * 2020: It along with a few other investors bought the |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/business/os-bz-red-lobster-thai-union-new-owner-20200831-njescwducfa35h5stjxifgd4fy-story.html |access-date=2022-07-15 |website=Orlando Sentinel |date=31 August 2020 |first=Austin|last=Fuller}} In May 2024, Red Lobster filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, announced the closure of at least 99 locations, and Thai Union issued the following statement: “After detailed analysis, we have determined that Red Lobster’s ongoing financial requirements no longer align with our capital allocation priorities and therefore are pursuing an exit of our minority investment.”{{Cite web |date=2024-05-14 |title=Red Lobster closing at least 99 locations as its future comes into question |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/business/consumer/red-lobster-closing-50-locations-what-cities-why-rcna152159 |access-date=2024-06-12 |website=NBC News |language=en}} == Issues == ===Labor=== ====Greenpeace accusations==== The Thai Union was investigated by Greenpeace, which showed a human trafficking report of Tier 3, meaning the company is not completely compliant with the standards. People are forced to work at sea for months, and sometimes years at a time. Being out at sea for long periods of time keeps them from being in contact with authorities, which allows the company to use such methods. They are going through forced labor, ultimately threatened with abuse, including getting beat with stingray tails, if they do not complete the tasks given to them by the Thai Union. The workers, who do not know any better, are being trafficked with no way of escaping.Greenpeace{{Better source needed|date=September 2025}} Thai Union released a statement in response to the accusations made by Greenpeace in 2015. It reiterated its commitment to human rights and the company's vision of "an industry that respects the oceans and protects marine life, offers safe employment for millions of people around the world, supports the development of coastal communities and continues to provide a safe, affordable and healthy food source for a global population well into the future."{{cite web|url=http://tu.listedcompany.com/newsroom/20151005-tu-pr01-en.pdf|title=THAI UNION STATEMENT|website=Thai Union|date=5 October 2015|accessdate=3 October 2017}} Thai Union also noted that it works closely with the [[International Seafood Sustainability Foundation|International Seafood Sustainability Foundation (ISSF)]] to "benefit the wider tuna fishing industry" and concluded by calling on Greenpeace to join the "industry debate that is already underway, to work towards achieving our shared objectives."{{cite news |last1=Kearns |first1=Madelyn |title=Thai Union responds to Greenpeace challenge |url=http://www.seafoodsource.com/news/environment-sustainability/thai-union-responds-to-greenpeace-challenge |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161028154118/http://www.seafoodsource.com/news/environment-sustainability/thai-union-responds-to-greenpeace-challenge |url-status=dead |archive-date=28 October 2016 |accessdate=20 June 2018 |work=Seafood Source |date=8 October 2015}} ====Slave labor and human rights==== Thai Union was named, but was not a defendant, in a lawsuit brought against [[Nestlé|Nestle Corporation]] for violating California laws.{{cite news|url=http://www.undercurrentnews.com/2015/08/28/thai-union-named-in-slavery-lawsuit-filed-against-nestle/|title=Thai Union named in slavery lawsuit filed against Nestle|work=Undercurrent News|date=28 August 2015|accessdate=17 September 2017}} Thai Union has been under scrutiny since the July 2015 publication of a ''New York Times'' article citing a former fisher stating he had been held captive on a vessel supplying a mother ship that ended up selling to Thai Union's [[Songkhla]] canning operation.{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/07/27/world/outlaw-ocean-thailand-fishing-sea-slaves-pets.html|title='Sea Slaves': The Human Misery That Feeds Pets and Livestock|first=Ian|last=Urbina|date=27 July 2015|work=The New York Times|accessdate=17 September 2017}} In a response to the ''New York Times'', the Thai Union re-asserted its commitment to the protection of human rights.[[Ian Urbina|Urbina, Ian.]] “[https://www.nytimes.com/2015/09/14/world/consumers-and-lawmakers-take-steps-to-end-forced-labor-in-fishing.html Consumers and Lawmakers Take Steps to End Forced Labor in Fishing] (Published 2015).” The New York Times, 13 Sept. 2015. Accessed 10 Jan. 2021. A spokesperson stated the company worked to prevent "any human trafficking or any human rights violation of any kind" highlighting procedures that are in place, such as routine audits of its canneries and boats in port to ensure against forced and child labor.{{cite web|url=http://tu.listedcompany.com/newsroom/20160615-tu-modern-slavery-en.pdf|title=Modern Slavery Act Transparency Statement 2016|website=Thai Union|accessdate=3 October 2017}} In 2015, the Thai Union released new codes of conduct, replacing the company's 2013 code of conduct. The "more stringent" new code of conduct allows for higher levels of "accountability and transparency" and showcased Thai Union's commitment to "earn the trust of customers, consumers and the world by operating with integrity and high ethical standards".{{cite news|url=https://www.undercurrentnews.com/2015/09/30/thai-union-looks-to-earn-trust-with-new-code-of-conduct/|title=Thai Union looks to earn trust with new code of conduct|work=Undercurrent News|date=30 September 2015|accessdate=17 September 2017}} The company also claims to have terminated relationships with 17 suppliers as a result of forced labor or human trafficking violations since the start of 2015, and have ended the use of employment brokers to source for workers for its seafood processing plants to stop [[debt bondage]].{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sustainable-business/2016/oct/07/cheap-seafood-fish-slavery-solutions-thailand-human-rights-abuse|title=Our love of cheap seafood is tainted by slavery: how can it be fixed?|first=Tom|last=Levitt|date=7 October 2016|work=The Guardian|accessdate=17 September 2017}} In December 2016, the Thai Union and the World Tuna Purse Seine Organization (WTPO) signed a [[memorandum of understanding]] (MOU) to establish a framework to ensure fair labor practices. The MOU includes the establishment and implementation of best practices on fair labor standards in operations.{{cite web|title=Thai Union signs fair labour pact|url=http://www.bangkokpost.com/business/news/1158157/thai-union-signs-fair-labour-pact|work=Bangkok Post|date=13 December 2016|accessdate=17 September 2017}} ====Slave labor in the shrimp industry==== Thailand's seafood industry, and by implication, the Thai Union, was the subject of a year-long study of the Thai shrimp industry commissioned by Nestlé. The report, conducted by Verité on behalf of Vevey-based Nestlé, was released on 23 November 2015. It found "indicators of forced labor, trafficking, and child labor to be present among sea-based and land-based workers."{{cite news|url=http://www.ibtimes.co.uk/nestle-admits-forced-labour-trafficking-child-labour-its-thai-seafood-supply-1530295|title=Nestlé admits forced labor, trafficking, and child labor in its Thai seafood supply|first=James|last=Tennent|date=24 November 2015|work=International Business Times|accessdate=17 September 2017}} In a statement issued on 10 December 2015, the Thai Union declared that it will cease working with all shrimp processing subcontractors by the end of 2015. The company said that it would bring all shrimp processing operations in-house to enable full oversight. All processing work will be directly controlled by the Thai Union to ensure that all workers, whether migrants or Thai, have safe, legal employment and are treated fairly and with dignity. Thai Union estimates that subcontractors employ about 1,000 migrant workers.{{cite web|url=https://www.nationthailand.com/news/business/corporate/30274659|title=TU acts to end worker mistreatment|work=The Nation|date=10 December 2015|access-date=17 September 2017}} Andy Hall, a British human rights defender and a migrant worker specialist based in Thailand, said that "Thai Union ... must be commended for belatedly moving seafood primary processing in house."{{cite news|url=http://www.bangkokpost.com/archive/activist-urges-eu-to-rethink-approach/794185|title=Activist urges EU to rethink approach|work=Bangkok Post|date=14 December 2015|accessdate=21 June 2018}} ===Environment=== ====Sourcing==== In October 2015 Greenpeace accused Thai Union subsidiary [[John West Foods|John West]] (UK) of making a "plainly false" claim that customers can trace its tuna back to the vessel that caught it. John West's website includes a tool that allows customers to enter the can code to "see exactly where your fish came from".{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2015/oct/14/john-west-tuna-greenpeace-challenges-tracing-claims|title=John West tuna: Greenpeace challenges tracing claims|agency=AP|date=14 October 2015|work=The Guardian|accessdate=17 September 2017}} The tool does not identify sources of Thai tuna and instead invites customers to email John West. John West said that the problem is a website limitation, and all its tuna is fully traceable.{{cite news|url=http://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/john-west-changes-website-after-10261635|title=John West changes website after Greenpeace accusations over traceability of tuna|first=Helen|last=Davies|date=14 October 2015|website=Liverpool Echo|accessdate=17 September 2017}} Greenpeace has also ranked [[John West Foods|John West]] last in sustainability surveys because 98 percent of its tuna was caught using "fish aggregation devices"{{cite web |author=Densham, Ariana|title=John West's broken promises|url=http://www.greenpeace.org.uk/blog/oceans/john-wests-broken-promises-20151008-0|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161028154327/http://www.greenpeace.org.uk/blog/oceans/john-wests-broken-promises-20151008-0|url-status=dead|archive-date=28 October 2016|website=Greenpeace|date=12 October 2015|accessdate=2018-06-21}} that kill other marine wildlife. Thai Union has committed to the following by 2020:{{cite web |url=http://sustainability.thaiunion.com/en/environment/responsible-sourcing |title=Responsible Sourcing | Thai Union Group Public Company Limited |accessdate=2016-10-28 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20161028152335/http://sustainability.thaiunion.com/en/environment/responsible-sourcing |archivedate=28 October 2016}} * Full traceability for all purchased seafood, reducing the risk of IUU fishing in the global fishing industry. Specific to its tuna business, Thai Union has committed to the following by 2020: * Digital traceability: We will work with innovative technology providers to develop a system for digital traceability. * Tuna sourcing policies: We will have aligned every one of our tuna sourcing policies everywhere in the world. We will publish these policies in line with our commitment to transparency. * Academic and scientific research: We will work with academic bodies, universities and scientific institutions to support research into fishery improvements. * Innovation: We have developed the Global Innovation Incubator in Thailand to look at all aspects of innovation and research into tuna from species to processing to packaging. * Post-harvest risk assessment: We will work with fishery experts to address the issues around tuna grading, utilization of non-target species and low-economic-value species, and care-of-catch to ensure high standards are met from harvest to plate. Thai Union Europe is working with [[World Wide Fund for Nature|WWF]]-UK and [[World Wide Fund for Nature|WWF]] France between 2014 and 2018 to improve the sustainability of seafood species and work towards [[Marine Stewardship Council|Marine Stewardship Council (MSC)]] certification and [[Aquaculture Stewardship Council|Aquaculture Stewardship Council (ASC)]] certification across the Thai Union Europe supply chain.{{cite web|url=http://assets.wwf.org.uk/downloads/wwf___thai_union_europe___partnership_progress_report_2016.pdf|title=WWF & THAI UNION EUROPE PARTNERSHIP PROGRESS REPORT 2016|website=Assets.wwf.org.uk|accessdate=3 October 2017}} In December 2016, Thai Union announced a strategy to ensure 100 percent of its branded tuna is sustainably sourced with a commitment of achieving a minimum of 75 percent by 2020. As part of the new tuna strategy, the Thai Union is investing US$90 million in initiatives that will increase the supply of sustainable tuna. This includes establishing 11 new fishery improvement projects (FIPs) around the world.{{cite news|url=http://www.intrafish.com/fisheries/1198856/thai-union-commits-to-100-percent-sustainable-tuna|title=Thai Union commits to 100% sustainable tuna|work=IntraFish|date=13 December 2016|accessdate=17 September 2017|url-access=subscription }}{{cite news|url=https://www.undercurrentnews.com/2016/12/13/thai-union-investing-90m-in-tuna-sustainability-initiatives/|title=Thai Union investing $90m in tuna sustainability initiatives|work=Undercurrent News|accessdate=17 September 2017}}{{cite web |url=http://www.fis.com/fis/worldnews/worldnews.asp?monthyear=&day=14&id=88817&l=e&special=&ndb=1%20target= |title=FIS - Worldnews - Thai Union aims to obtain all its tuna from sustainable sources |accessdate=2016-12-16 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20161214172703/http://www.fis.com/fis/worldnews/worldnews.asp?monthyear=&day=14&id=88817&l=e&special=&ndb=1%20target= |archivedate=14 December 2016}}{{cite web|url=http://www.just-food.com/news/thai-union-makes-sustainable-tuna-sourcing-pledge_id135252.aspx|title=Thai Union makes sustainable tuna sourcing pledge|date=13 December 2016|website=Just-food|accessdate=17 September 2017|archive-date=13 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170913230849/https://www.just-food.com/news/thai-union-makes-sustainable-tuna-sourcing-pledge_id135252.aspx|url-status=dead}}{{cite web |url=http://www.seafoodsource.com/news/foodservice-retail/thai-union-commits-to-sustainable-tuna-targets-75-percent-by-2020 |title=Thai Union commits to sustainable tuna, targets 75 percent by 2020 - SeafoodSource.com |accessdate=2016-12-16 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20161214185212/http://www.seafoodsource.com/news/foodservice-retail/thai-union-commits-to-sustainable-tuna-targets-75-percent-by-2020 |archivedate=14 December 2016}}{{cite web|url=http://www.sustainablebrands.com/news_and_views/business_models/sustainable_brands/thai_union_commits_100_sustainable_tuna_can_it_get|title=Thai Union Commits to 100% Sustainable Tuna, But Can It Get There?|website=Sustainable Brands|date=13 December 2016|accessdate=17 September 2017}} In December 2016, eight of the world's largest seafood companies, including the Thai Union, issued a 10-point statement committing to action on ocean stewardship following the first "keystone dialogue" between scientists and business leaders. The companies committed to improving transparency and traceability, and reducing illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing in their supply chains.{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-environment-fishing-seafood/big-seafood-companies-promise-to-reduce-illegal-fishing-idUSKBN14322I|title=Big seafood companies promise to reduce illegal fishing|date=14 December 2016|work=Reuters|accessdate=17 September 2017}}{{cite web|url=http://www.thaiunion.com/en/newsroom/press-release/433/keystone-dialogue-between-scientists-and-seafood-industry-leaders-creates-breakthrough-in-ocean-stewardship|title="Keystone Dialogue" between Scientists and Seafood Industry Leaders Creates Breakthrough in Ocean Stewardship|website=Thai Union|type=Press release|accessdate=17 September 2017}} In December 2016, Greenpeace reported that the Thai Union subsidiary, Lucky Union Foods Co. Ltd. (LUF), purchased [[surimi]] base from Pacific Marine Food Products Co. Ltd., a company which confirmed that it had sourced from "vessels of concern". LUF also supplied shaped surimi to Thai Union Manufacturing Co. Ltd. (TUM) for use in pet foods.{{cite book|title=Turn The Tide; Human Rights Abuses and Illegal Fishing in Thailand's Overseas Fishing Industry|date=December 2016|publisher=Greenpeace Southeast Asia|location=Bangkok|url=http://www.greenpeace.org/seasia/PageFiles/745330/Turn-The-Tide.pdf|accessdate=16 December 2016}} In February 2017, the Thai Union 2015 Sustainability Report earned the number one ranking in Asia for sustainability reporting in the Top 100 Seafood Firms' Transparency Benchmark from Seafood Intelligence, a global news service that reports on the seafood sector and evaluates the industry's sustainability data and transparency levels.{{cite web|url=http://www.thaiunion.com/en/newsroom/press-release/455/thai-union-tops-in-asia-for-csr-and-sustainability-in-latest-seafood-intelligence-top-100-report|title=Thai Union Tops in Asia for CSR and Sustainability in Latest Seafood Intelligence Top 100 Report|website=Thai Union|type=Press release|accessdate=17 September 2017}} In March 2017, Thai Union and the United States Agency for International Development Oceans and Fisheries Partnership ([[United States Agency for International Development|USAID]] Oceans) announced a partnership to combat [[illegal, unreported, and unregulated fishing|illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing]], promote fair and ethical seafood supply chains, and improve the sustainability of fisheries in the Asia-Pacific region.{{cite web|url=http://www.thaiunion.com/en/newsroom/press-release/464/usaid-and-thai-union-partner-to-implement-digital-traceability-to-combat-illegal-fishing-in-the-asia-pacific-region|title=USAID and Thai Union partner to implement digital traceability to combat illegal fishing in the Asia Pacific Region|website=Thai Union|type=Press release|accessdate=17 September 2017}} In June 2017, at a [[World Economic Forum]] (WEF) meeting in New York City, the Thai Union committed to the WEF's Tuna 2020 Traceability Declaration. The declaration supports the United Nations (UN) [[Sustainable Development Goals]] (SDGs) which were adopted by all 193 heads of state via a UN Resolution in September 2015 at a United Nations summit.{{cite web|url=http://www.thaiunion.com/en/newsroom/press-release/492/thai-union-commits-to-world-economic-forums-tuna-2020-traceability-declaration|title=Thai Union Commits to World Economic Forum's Tuna 2020 Traceability Declaration|website=Thai Union|type=Press release|accessdate=17 September 2017}} In June 2017, Thai Union Group signed a pledge as part of its membership in the Seafood Business for Ocean Stewardship (SeaBOS), committing to improve operations as well as challenge the rest of the seafood industry to follow, all with the goal of helping the world achieve the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).{{cite web|url=http://www.thaiunion.com/en/newsroom/press-release/498/thai-union-commits-to-ambitious-seabos-ocean-stewardship-pledge|title=Thai Union Commits to Ambitious SeaBOS Ocean Stewardship Pledge|website=Thai Union|type=Press release|accessdate=17 September 2017}} In July 2017, Thai Union Group committed to measures that will tackle [[illegal fishing]] and [[overfishing]], as well as improve the livelihoods of hundreds of thousands of workers throughout the company's supply chains, in an agreement with Greenpeace. Greenpeace and the Thai Union agreed to meet every six months to assess the company's progress and implementation.{{cite web|url=http://www.thaiunion.com/en/newsroom/press-release/505/thai-union-commits-to-more-sustainable-socially-responsible-seafood|title=Thai Union Commits to More Sustainable, Socially-Responsible Seafood|website=Thai Union|type=Press release|accessdate=17 September 2017}} In October 2017, a memorandum of understanding (MoU) was signed between WWF, Thai Union Europe, ACTEMSA S.A., and Industrias Alimenticias Leal Santos LTDA, to launch a Fishery Improvement Project (FIP) for the pole and line skipjack, yellowfin, and bigeye tuna fishery in the south and southeast coastal areas of Brazil. The aim of the FIP is to meet the standards of the Marine Stewardship Council (MSC), which assesses whether a fishery is well-managed and sustainable.{{Cite web|url=https://www.thaiunion.com/en/newsroom/press-release/550/mou-for-new-brazil-fip-signed|title=MoU for New Brazil FIP Signed|website=www.thaiunion.com|language=en|access-date=2019-10-15}} In March 2018, Thai Union Group joined forces with the Global Ghost Gear Initiative (GGGI) in a drive to reduce the growing problem of abandoned, lost, and discarded fishing gear (ALDFG) worldwide.{{Cite web|url=https://www.thaiunion.com/en/newsroom/press-release/793/thai-union-joins-initiative-to-help-combat-marine-plastics|title=Thai Union Joins Initiative to Help Combat Marine Plastics|website=www.thaiunion.com|language=en|access-date=2019-10-15}} ===Others=== ====Bumble Bee Foods==== In December 2014, Thai Union announced it would spend US$1.5 billion to acquire [[Bumble Bee Foods]]. That deal was put in jeopardy after the US Department of Justice announced it began an anti-trust investigation into the company's over-pricing and competitive practices. Thai Union abandoned its purchase plans in early December 2015 after US officials objected on the grounds that it would reduce competition. "Consumers are better off without this deal," Bill Baer, assistant attorney general of the US Department of Justice's antitrust division, said...."Our investigation convinced us—and the parties knew or should have known from the get-go — that the market is not functioning competitively today, and further consolidation would only make things worse."{{cite news|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/news/big-tuna-chicken-of-the-sea-wont-net-bumble-bee/|title=Big tuna: Chicken of the Sea won't net Bumble Bee|work=CBS News|accessdate=17 September 2017}} ====Dow Jones Sustainability Index (DJSI) Emerging Markets==== In September 2017, Thai Union was named to the Dow Jones Sustainability Index (DJSI) Emerging Markets for the fourth year in a row. Thai Union's sustainability strategy, SeaChange®, successfully drove the score with industry best-in-class 100th percentile rankings for Climate Strategy, Materiality, Human Capital Development, Health and Nutrition, Water Related Risks, and Policy Influence.{{Cite web|url=https://www.thaiunion.com/en/newsroom/press-release/522/thai-union-named-to-dow-jones-sustainability-index-for-fourth-consecutive-year|title=Thai Union Named to Dow Jones Sustainability Index for Fourth Consecutive Year|website=www.thaiunion.com|language=en|access-date=2019-10-15}} ====FTSE4Good Emerging Index==== In January 2017, the Thai Union was named to the FTSE4Good Emerging Index by [[FTSE Russell]]. The FTSE4Good Emerging Index is an extension of the [[FTSE4Good Index]] Series—the latter of which was launched in 2001 to help investors integrate environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors into their investment decisions and as a framework for corporate engagement and stewardship.{{cite web|url=http://www.thaiunion.com/en/newsroom/press-release/441/thai-union-added-to-ftse4good-emerging-index|title=Thai Union Added to FTSE4Good Emerging Index|website=Thai Union|type=Press release|accessdate=17 September 2017}} ==See also== * [[Simplot]] * [[Bolton Group]] * [[Itochu]] * [[FCF Co, Ltd.]] ==References== {{Reflist}} [[Category:Companies established in 1988]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand]] [[Category:Companies in the SET50]] [[Category:1988 establishments in Thailand]] [[Category:Fish processing companies]] [[Category:Seafood companies of Asia]] [[Category:Fishing in Thailand]] [[Category:Food and drink companies of Thailand]]

Thai Union Group PCL is a Thailand-based producer of seafood based products. It was founded in 1977, and was listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) on 22 November 1994.
Thai Union operates worldwide with plant facilities in France, Germany, Ghana, Poland, Portugal, Papua New Guinea, Norway, Seychelles, Scotland, Vietnam, Thailand and the United States. Its business includes tuna, shrimp, sardines, mackerel, salmon, pet food and prepared foods.
